newsitem.title: UK: Railtrack up on bear squeeze.
newsitem.headline: Railtrack up on bear squeeze.

text.p: Shares in Britain's Railtrack jumped over five percent on Thursday to a near record high as continued investment demand led to a shortage of stock in the market, dealers said.
By 1515 GMT the stock was up 25-1/2p at 396, just short of Wednesday's record high of 396-1/2. Volume was an active 4.4 million shares.
"There is a big bear squeeze," said the head of equity trading at a major brokerage.
"We saw some demand yesterday and that's created a squeeze in the stock. We've always had it as a "Buy" because it is fundamentally cheap. We've always thought it is massively undervalued," he added.
Traders said the stock had been buoyed in recent weeks by talk of a revaluation of the company's substantial property portfolio.
There was also talk of some U.S. investment interest.
"U.S. utilities have been buying the U.K. and the theory is there has been some buying of bits and pieces of Railtrack," one trader said.
Fellow privatised utility London Electricity was the latest utility to fall into the hands of acquisitive U.S. firms on Wednesday when it agreed to a bid by Entergy Corp.
There are now only two independent regional electricity companies remaining.
